explanation: Sort copies by start, then extend the current output interval while the next interval begins no later than its end.
correctness: Once intervals are sorted, a gap before the next start means no later interval can bridge it. Otherwise joining the ranges preserves exactly their union.
walkthrough: Sort [[9,12],[1,4],[4,7],[10,14]] by start to obtain [1,4], [4,7], [9,12], [10,14]. The first two touch and become [1,7]. The last two overlap and become [9,14]. The gap from 7 to 9 remains, giving [[1,7],[9,14]] in newly allocated meeting objects. JSON intervals are [StartTime,EndTime] pairs; return newly allocated Meeting objects in increasing start order and preserve the supplied list and objects.
edgeCases: Touching [1,4] and [4,7] merge to [1,7]. An interval contained in another adds no extent; empty input returns an empty new list.
timeComplexity: O(n log n+n) time: sort n meeting references by start, then process each once.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the sorted reference copy and up to n newly allocated result intervals; original intervals are untouched.
